info.title: Pyo API
info.description:
Everything the dashboard does, for scripts. Read with GET, and change things with one operation per POST to `/ops`.

Authenticate with an API key from the dashboard's API keys page: `Authorization: Bearer pyo_…`. A key acts as you, with your role in each team, and is limited further by its access: **read** (look, never change), **deploy** (also deploy, roll back, restart, stop and scale services) or **full** (everything you can do in its teams). Each endpoint and operation says the access it needs in `x-pyo-access`.

Errors come back as `{"error": "…"}` with a status code. Times are milliseconds since 1970 unless they say otherwise.

get.description:
One snapshot of every team you're in (or the API key's teams): their
projects, services and deployments, clusters and servers, domains,
certificates, volumes, backups, registry logins, builders and recent
activity. The dashboard renders from this, and scripts can read it too.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: The snapshot: `user`, `teams`, `projects`, `services`, `deployments`, `clusters`, `servers` and the rest, each a list.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
The account these credentials act as: an API key's owner, or the person
who connected an assistant.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: Your account.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
Its version, and the features a hosted Pyo turned on (none when
self-hosted). No API key needed.

No API key needed.

200.description: The version and features.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

post.description:
Every change goes through here: one operation per request, named by
`op`, with its fields. Ids of new things are chosen by you (the kind's
prefix and `_`, then 4 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dashes or
underscores), so a retried request can't create something twice. Each
operation says which API key access it needs. Operations on your account
and on this installation aren't open to API keys and aren't listed.

API key access: each operation says what it needs (**deploy** or **full**).

200.description: Done. Always `ok: true`, and some operations add more, such as a new API key or a join command.

400.description: Not a known operation, a missing field, or a value Pyo can't accept.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

403.description: Your role in the team, or the API key's access, doesn't allow it.

404.description: The team or the thing it names doesn't exist, or isn't yours to see.

409.description: It conflicts with what's there, such as a name already taken.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

502.description: An outside service it needed (a secret store, a registry) refused or failed.

503.description: This installation isn't set up to store the secret it would save.

get.description:
The last lines each of a service's replicas printed, read from its
cluster on request. Takes up to 15 seconds.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: The lines.

404.description: No such service, or it isn't yours to see.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster didn't answer within 15 seconds (is it connected?).

get.description:
Its backups in the team's restic repository, newest first, read from
its cluster on request (a short job there). Takes up to two minutes.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `snapshots`: each one's `id`, `shortId`, `time` and `sizeBytes`, newest first.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such volume, or it isn't yours to see.

409.description: The team has no backups, or its backup store can't be reached from the volume's cluster.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster didn't answer in time (is it connected?).

delete.description:
Deletes one of a volume's backups from the team's restic repository,
with a short job on its cluster that waits for the volume's other
backups and restores. The space it held is freed shortly after. Deleting
one that's already gone succeeds. Owners and admins.

API key access: **full**.

parameters.name: snapshotId
parameters.description: The snapshot's id, or its short id (see listVolumeSnapshots).

200.description: `ok`: deleted (or already gone).

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

403.description: Only owners and admins, with an API key that has full access.

404.description: No such volume, or it isn't yours to see.

409.description: The team has no backups, or its backup store can't be reached from the volume's cluster.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster didn't answer in time (is it connected?).

A cron job's recent runs, newest first: when each started and finished,

get.description:
CPU, memory, disk and network over time for a team's servers and
services, sampled once a minute. Servers also get load and disk reads
and writes. Each series lines up with `times`, with `null` where nothing
was measured.

API key access: **read**.

Visits, requests, errors, response times, countries, pages and referrers
for a team's websites: all of them, one project's, one service's, or one
domain.

API key access: **read**.

parameters.description: Only this project's sites: its id, or "all".

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: Only this domain: its id, or "all".

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Only this service's domains: its id.

get.description:
The web server's log of requests to a team's websites, newest first,
filtered like the traffic figures.

API key access: **read**.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Only this project's sites: its id, or "all".

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: Only this domain: its id, or "all".

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Only this service's domains: its id.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only requests before this time, in milliseconds: for the next page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many, 1 to 500 (100 by default).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only one class of status: "1xx" to "5xx".

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only requests whose URL or host contains this (any case).

200.description: `logs` (newest first: time, method, host, path, status, duration, size, country, device and address as the IP setting allows), `next` (the `before` for the next page, or null), `ipMode`, and on the first page a `summary` of the filtered requests.

404.description: No such team, or you aren't in it.

503.description: This installation doesn't store request logs.

get.description:
Connections to a service's public TCP and UDP ports through the
gateway: per port, over time, by country and outcome ("ok", "blocked" by an
IP rule, "limited" by the connection limit, "unreachable" when the service
didn't answer), and the latest 50. A connection is counted when it
closes (a UDP exchange after a minute without packets). Ports that bypass
the gateway aren't counted.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `ports`, `series`, `countries`, `outcomes`, `recent` (address as the IP setting allows) and `ipMode`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such service, or you can't see it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
What a service's firewall turned away: website requests (a 403, or a
429 over a rate limit) and connections to TCP ports through the gateway.
It shows them over time (`series`), per rule, per source, country and
website path, and the latest 50. A rule is its id, or "blocked" or
"rate-limit" when no rule matches the source now. UDP ports and ports
that bypass the gateway aren't counted.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `total`, `series`, `rules`, `sources` (address as the IP setting allows), `countries`, `paths`, `recent` and `ipMode`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such service, or you can't see it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
The address (and its country) Pyo sees your requests come from, so the
dashboard can warn before a firewall rule would shut you out.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `ip` and `country` (a two-letter code, or empty when unknown).

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
What a service's web application firewall found: requests it blocked,
and ones it only logged in log-only mode. It shows them over time
(`series`), per rule, domain, source, country and path, and the latest
50 with the rules that matched. `custom` shows how often each custom
rule matched, by its number. Query strings are kept with sensitive
values redacted.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `blocked`, `logged`, `clients`, `series`, `rules`, `hosts`, `sources`, `countries`, `paths`, `recent`, `custom` and `ipMode`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such service, or you can't see it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
Every image a team's services deployed, by repository, with each
version's deployments, the services that used it and whether one runs it
now.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: The images.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such team, or you aren't in it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
Pyo's registry, where the images it builds from Git and the team's own
pushes are kept, as one team sees it: its address, where it runs (when the team has that
cluster), whether Pyo reaches it, the space the team's images take, the
team's repositories (tags, size, last build) and its cleanup: how many
deployments' images are kept per service, and when images were last
removed (within the last week). Read only.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `address` (in the cluster only, where servers pull from), `location` (`clusterId` and `server`, or null), `reachable`, `usedBytes`, `repositories`, `retainDeployments`, `lastCleanupAt`, `pushAddress`, `teamPath` and `tokens`. Each of `repositories` has `repository` (as servers pull it), `tailnetRepository`, `kind` ("built" or "pushed"), `serviceId`, `tags`, `bytes` and `lastPushAt`. `tailnetRepository` is a pushed repository's name on the team's tailnet, `<pushAddress>/<team>/<project>/<service>`. It's null for one Pyo built, or without a tailnet. `pushAddress` is the registry's address on the team's tailnet, where the team pushes and pulls its own images, or null without a tailnet. Each of `tokens` has `id`, `name`, `scope`, `createdBy`, `createdAt`, `expiresAt` and `lastUsedAt`, but never the token itself.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such team, or you aren't in it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
A team's Postgres and MySQL databases and Valkey
(Redis-compatible) KV databases: engine, version, size, instances, the cluster's status (phase,
primary, ready instances, failovers), the services connected to each and
their variables, passwords masked.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `databases`, each with `id`, `name`, `engine`, `version`, `size`, `cpu`, `memory`, `storageGi`, `instances`, `pooler`, `rest`, `deletionProtection`, `status` (with `backup`: `firstRecoverabilityPoint`, `lastSuccessfulBackup`, `lastArchivedWal`, `lastFailedBackup`, `message`), `backup`, `restoredFrom`, `readReplicas`, `extensions`, `setup`, `members`, `connections` and `variables` (passwords masked). `backup` has `enabled`, `retentionDays` and `hour` for Postgres and MySQL. For KV, once turned on, it has `enabled`, `schedule`, `hour`, `keep` and `backupDatabaseId` (its id in Backups). `readReplicas` is null when off, or has `instances`, `ready`, `reported` and `members` (each with `name`, `ready`, `server` and `lagSeconds`). `extensions` is null for MySQL. For Postgres and KV, it lists each extension or module that's on or being turned off, with `name`, `enabled`, `state` ("enabled", "pending", "restarting", "disabling" or "failed") and a `message`. `setup` is null once the cluster's databases are set up. While they're being set up or updated, it has `state` ("installing" or "failed") and a `message`. `members` lists each instance's `name`, `role` ("primary" or "replica"), `ready` and the `server` it runs on, primary first.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such team, or you aren't in it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
One Postgres, MySQL or KV database, as `listDatabases` lists them.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: The database, as in `listDatabases`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such database, or you can't see it.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
The extensions Pyo's databases offer: Postgres extensions and KV
modules. Each one's `name`, `engine` ("postgres" or "valkey"), `section`
("managed" ones are turned on with `setDatabaseExtensions`, and the
database's owner adds "additional" ones with CREATE EXTENSION), a
one-line `description`, its `docs`, its `edition` when it's a limited build,
`hidden` when it's obsolete (shown only while a database has it on), and
whether turning it on or off `restart`s the database (every KV module
does).

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `extensions`: each one's `name`, `engine` ("postgres" or "valkey"), `section`, `description`, `docs`, `edition` (when it's a limited build), `hidden` (when it's obsolete) and `restart`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

get.description:
The recent output of each of its parts, oldest first: `at`, `level`,
`source` (the instance), `role` ("primary", "replica", "read",
"pooler", "read-pooler", "sentinel", "proxy" (KV's endpoint) or "other"), `message`, and
`raw` for structured lines. `events`: what happened to it, newest first.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `logs`, `events` and `fetchedAt`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such database, or you aren't in its team.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster's agent didn't answer in time.

get.description:
Its health over time, sampled about every 30 seconds. Per member
(`members`: each instance, read replica, pooler and KV endpoint), its
`role`, `server`, and series for `cpu` in cores, `memoryMi`,
`diskUsedGi` (only where the volume reports its own space),
`connections` and `lagSeconds`. For the whole database, `transactions`
(Postgres), `queries` (MySQL), `poolerQueries` and `commands` (KV) per
second, `connections` (`primary`, `replicas`, `limit`, and the pooler's
`poolerActive`, `poolerWaiting`, `poolerServersActive`,
`poolerServersIdle` and `poolerMaxWaitSeconds`), `cacheHitRatio`,
`keyHitRatio`, `evictions` per second, `routing` (KV reads per second
served by `replica`s or the `primary`, and `fallbacks` to the primary)
and `storage` (`sizeBytes`, `memoryUsedBytes`, `maxmemoryBytes`,
`keys`). Each series lines up with `times`, with `null` where nothing
was measured. A series is `null` when the database doesn't report it.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `range`, `stepMs`, `times` (milliseconds), `engine`, `members` and the database's series.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such database, or you aren't in its team.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

post.description:
Checks the admin login from the cluster, makes a backup user with it,
then saves the database and its schedule. Team owners and admins.

API key access: **deploy**.

200.description: Saved: `ok` and the new database's `id`.

400.description: A missing or wrong value, or the login didn't work.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

403.description: You aren't an owner or admin of the team, or the API key can only read.

404.description: No such team or service.

409.description: The team already backs up a database by that name.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster didn't finish checking in time (is it connected?).

post.description:
Everything `startDatabaseImport` checks, without importing. The cluster
connects to the source, which must be reachable from there, and checks
the login, TLS, its version, its extensions and that every table is
readable. It also checks that the database to import into is empty.
Owners and admins.

API key access: **full**.

200.description: It can be imported: `source` (`version`, `sizeBytes`), and `extensions`: `turnedOn` (Pyo turns them on first) and `madeByImport`.

400.description: Why not: the URL, the source can't be reached or refuses the login, TLS, its version, an extension Pyo's Postgres doesn't have.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

409.description: The database to import into isn't empty, or is importing.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster didn't answer in time (is it connected?).

post.description:
Copies a Postgres or MySQL database into one of the team's: a new one
(`newDatabase`), or an empty one (`databaseId`). From `url` (the source
must be reachable from the cluster) or `uploadId` (a dump uploaded
first). It's checked first, as `checkDatabaseImport`. Then the
database's `import` shows how it goes ("pending", "running", "succeeded"
or "failed", with a `phase`), and its logs have the import's output.
Writes made to the source during the import aren't copied. Owners and
admins.

API key access: **full**.

200.description: Started: `importId`, `databaseId`, `clusterId`, and what the check found (`source`, `extensions`).

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

403.description: You aren't an owner or admin of the team, or the API key can't make changes.

409.description: The database isn't empty or is importing, or the name is taken.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

504.description: The cluster didn't answer in time (is it connected?).

post.description:
Runs a failed import again, from the same source. After a failure, Pyo
keeps the URL's password (sealed), and an uploaded dump for
`PYO_DATABASE_IMPORT_RETENTION_HOURS` (24 by default). A new database
made for the import is made again. A database that already existed must
still be empty. Owners and admins.

API key access: **full**.

200.description: Started again: the new `importId`.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

409.description: It didn't fail, there's a newer one, or the dump is gone.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

post.description:
The first step of uploading a dump to import: say what it is and get
where to send it. Then `PUT` the file to `uploadUrl` as it is, before
`expiresAt`, with exactly the `headers` given and nothing else. Send no
cookies or API key, since the URL may be on another host. Then call
`startDatabaseImport` with `uploadId`. Postgres takes `.sql`, `.sql.gz`
or a custom-format `.dump` (pg_dump -Fc). MySQL takes `.sql` or
`.sql.gz` (mysqldump). The dump stays in the team's storage in Pyo until
its import succeeds, or for `PYO_DATABASE_IMPORT_RETENTION_HOURS` (24 by
default) when unused. At most `PYO_DATABASE_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` (10 GiB by
default). Owners and admins.

API key access: **full**.

200.description: `uploadId` (for `startDatabaseImport`), and where to send the file: `uploadUrl` (relative to your Pyo's address when it starts with `/`), `method` ("PUT"), `headers` (send exactly these) and `expiresAt` (start sending before it).

400.description: Not a file Pyo can import, by its name, or empty.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

403.description: You aren't an owner or admin of the team, or the API key can't make changes.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

503.description: This installation has no storage for uploads.

put.description:
The second step: the file, as the request's body, to the `uploadUrl`
that `createDatabaseDumpUpload` gave (its `token` is the only
credential: send no API key). Once only, before its `expiresAt`, and
exactly the size declared.

No API key needed.

200.description: Stored: `uploadId`, `size`, `sha256`, `format`, `extensions` (Postgres: the ones it makes) and `sourceVersion` (what it was dumped from, when it says).

400.description: Not the size declared, or not what its name says.

403.description: The token is wrong, used already or expired.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

503.description: This installation has no storage for uploads.

The repositories the team's GitHub installations can see, to deploy
from.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: `repositories`: each with `installationId`, `account`, `fullName`, `name`, `private`, `defaultBranch`, `htmlUrl` and `pushedAt`.

The file a Git build of a repository would use by default: its Dockerfile,
else its Containerfile, in the build context. None: the build is

parameters.name: repo

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The build context, a folder of the repository ("." for its root).

200.description: `file`: "Dockerfile" or "Containerfile" (a Dockerfile wins when there are both), or null when there's neither.

400.description: No `team`, `repo` or `branch`, or the team hasn't connected GitHub.

post.description:
What importing a Compose file would create: a project, and a service per
Compose service with its source, ports, variables, volumes and health
check, in deploy order. It adds a warning for each thing that isn't
carried over. Nothing is created. Edit the plan if you like, then pass it
to the `importCompose` operation.

API key access: **read**.

200.description: The plan.

400.description: Not a Compose file Pyo can read, nothing importable, or no file given.

401.description: No API key, or not a valid one (revoked, expired or mistyped).

404.description: No such team, cluster or file.

500.description: Something went wrong on Pyo's side. It's logged.

name.description: A name for it, unique in the team.

clusterId.description: The cluster that reaches it and runs its backups.

serviceId.description: The Pyo service it is, if it is one.

database.description: The database to back up. Not needed for Redis.

adminUser.description: A login allowed to create users: Pyo makes a backup user with it and doesn't keep it.

hour.description: The hour of day it runs, 0 to 23 (UTC).

keep.description: How many backups to keep, 1 to 365.

AddFirewallRuleOp.title: Add firewall rule
AddFirewallRuleOp.description:
Add an access rule to the end of a service's firewall. Allow and block rules are checked in order, and the first match decides. With no match, the client gets in. Rate limit rules then apply to websites, and each matching one counts the request, per client address and per server.

API key access: **full**.

id.description: A new id you choose: `fwr_` then 4 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dashes or underscores.

operator.description: "in" (the default) or "notIn": whether the client's address or country is in `sources`.

sources.description: Up to 50 IP addresses and ranges ("198.51.100.0/24", "2001:db8::/32") or two-letter country codes ("DE"), but not both. None (with "in") matches any client. Countries apply to websites only, since TCP and UDP ports never see a client's country. Rate limits take no countries, and only one value with "notIn".

requests.description: A rate limit's requests from each client address per `per`: 1 to 1,000,000.

per.description: A rate limit's window: "second" or "minute" (the default).

AddVolumeOp.title: Add volume
AddVolumeOp.description:
Add a persistent volume to a service, mounted at `mountPath` from its next deploy.

API key access: **full**.

id.description: A new id you choose: `vol_` then 4 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dashes or underscores.

AddWafRuleOp.title: Add waf rule
AddWafRuleOp.description:

AttachVolumeOp.title: Attach volume
AttachVolumeOp.description:
Attach a detached volume to a service on its cluster, mounted at `mountPath` from the service's next deploy.
A service of another project (or any project, for a volume whose project was deleted) gets the volume moved into its project first, data, id and backups kept: the volume shows `moving` until its cluster has moved it, then it's attached (or `moveError` says why not). A volume can't move to another cluster.
A volume on a one-server storage class keeps its data on that server, so the service must be able to run there.

API key access: **full**.

Autoscale.description:

replica reserves. The target that asks for more replicas wins.

ConnectDatabaseOp.title: Connect database
ConnectDatabaseOp.description:
Connect a service to a database on its cluster. Postgres adds DATABASE_URL (through the pooler when it's on) and DATABASE_URL_DIRECT, plus DATABASE_URL_READ with read replicas. MySQL adds DATABASE_URL (mysql://, to the primary), MYSQL_HOST, MYSQL_PORT, MYSQL_USER, MYSQL_PASSWORD and MYSQL_DATABASE. KV adds REDIS_URL (which follows failover and sends reads to read replicas), plus KV_REST_API_URL, KV_REST_API_TOKEN and KV_REST_API_READ_ONLY_TOKEN (reads only) with its REST API. With `env`, it adds only those, under the service's own names. With `prefix`, it adds all of them with that prefix, so two databases' variables don't clash. They're secret variables and apply on the service's next deploy.

API key access: **full**.

env.description: The service's own names for them: `{"WORDPRESS_DB_HOST": "MYSQL_HOST", …}`, each a variable the database offers, or several joined by ":" (`MYSQL_HOST:MYSQL_PORT`). Under its own names, Postgres also offers POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_DATABASE (the primary, not the pooler), and KV REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT and REDIS_PASSWORD. Kept, so they follow its changes.

prefix.description: Instead of `env`: all its variables, each named with this prefix (`MYSQL` gives MYSQL_DATABASE_URL…), so a service can use databases whose variables would clash.

CreateDatabaseOp.title: Create database
CreateDatabaseOp.description:
Create a Postgres, MySQL or KV (Redis-compatible key-value, Valkey) database on one of the team's clusters. The first database on a cluster also sets up databases there, which takes a minute or two. `size` sets CPU and memory per instance: "small" (0.25 CPU, 512 MiB, 5 GiB), "medium" (0.5, 1 GiB, 10 GiB), "large" (1, 2 GiB, 20 GiB) or "xlarge" (2, 4 GiB, 50 GiB). MySQL needs 1 GiB, so "medium" or larger. `instances` is 1 for a single server with no automatic failover. For high availability, use a primary and 2 to 8 replicas for Postgres (instances 3 to 9), 2 to 4 for KV (3 to 5), or 2 or 4 for MySQL (3 or 5). A replica takes over when the primary's server is lost. MySQL has no pooler, read replicas or REST API. Developers and up.

API key access: **full**.

id.description: A new id you choose: `mdb_` then 4 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dashes or underscores.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, unique in the team.

instances.description: 1 (a single server), or high availability: 3 to 9 for Postgres (2 to 8 replicas), 3 to 5 for KV (2 to 4), 3 or 5 for MySQL (2 or 4).

version.description: Postgres "16", "17" or "18" (the default). MySQL "8.4". Valkey "8.0" or "8.1" (the default).

storageGi.description: Storage per instance in GiB. Defaults to the size's storage.

pooler.description: Postgres: a connection pooler in front (on by default).

rest.description: KV: a REST API, for serverless and edge code.

cpuMillis.description: A custom size's CPU per instance in millicores: 125 to 8000, in steps of 125.

memoryMi.description: A custom size's memory per instance in MiB: 512 (Postgres), 1024 (MySQL) or 256 (KV) to 32768, in steps of 256.

readReplicas.description: Dedicated read replicas: 0 (the default) to 5 for Postgres, or to 4 for KV. MySQL has none.

extensions.description: Postgres extensions or KV modules to turn on with it, from `listDatabaseExtensions` with `section` "managed" for its engine. For example ["vector", "pg_cron"] or ["valkey-json"].

A push needs that project and service to exist. It works over HTTPS from a device on the installation's tailnet. Team owners and admins. The token comes back only once, with the username, address and team path to log in and push with.

CreateServiceOp.title: Create service
CreateServiceOp.description:
Create a service and deploy it.

API key access: **full**.

service.description:
The service, as in the snapshot's services: id (`svc_…`), projectId, clusterId, name, source, ports, env and the rest.
A template's service records where it came from in `source`: `templateVersion`, `appVersion`, `images` (each Compose service's image, `repository:tag@digest`, by name) and `fields` (the deploy form's values, with a secret one only as `{"secret": true, "set": …, "env": …}`). Saves keep them. Responses add `customized` when its image is no longer the template's.
Its ports: `name`, `containerPort`, `protocol` ("HTTP", "TCP" or "UDP"), `exposure` ("internal", "http" for a website, "nodeport", or "loadbalancer" for a public TCP or UDP port) and `publicPort`.
A public TCP or UDP port goes through the gateway unless `proxy` is false. Then, for TCP only, it can have `ipFilter` (`{"mode": "allow" or "deny", "cidrs": [...]}`), `connectionLimit` (open connections on the port, from everyone together), `sendProxyProtocol` ("V1" or "V2", to the service) and `acceptProxyProtocol` (read the visitor's address from a header sent by a load balancer in front, while connections without one still work). Ports 22, 53, 80, 443 and a few others can't be public. Each public port belongs to one service on its cluster.

deploymentId.description: A new id you choose for its first deployment: `dpl_` then 4 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dashes or underscores.

databases.description: Databases to connect it to before its first deploy, as `connectDatabase` does: each `{"id": "mdb_…", "env": {"WORDPRESS_DB_HOST": "MYSQL_HOST", …}}` (`env` optional).

SetDatabaseBackupsOp.title: Set database backups
SetDatabaseBackupsOp.description:
Turn a database's backups on or off, to the team's Backups destination. Postgres: every change archived continuously and a base backup daily, so it can be restored to any moment in the last `retentionDays`. MySQL: a full backup daily with the changes since the last one, so it can be restored to any moment in the last `retentionDays` up to its latest backup. Both are stored in the team's folder of the destination. KV: a snapshot `schedule`d daily or weekly, the last `keep` kept, listed in Backups with the team's other databases. Developers and up.

API key access: **full**.

retentionDays.description: Postgres and MySQL: 1 to 90, 7 by default.

hour.description: The hour backups run, 0 to 23 (UTC). Defaults to 3 for Postgres and MySQL, and 2 for KV.

keep.description: KV: how many snapshots to keep, 1 to 365, 14 by default.

SetDatabaseExtensionsOp.title: Set database extensions
SetDatabaseExtensionsOp.description:
Turn a Postgres database's extensions or a KV database's modules on and off. `extensions` is the full list to have on, from `listDatabaseExtensions` with `section` "managed" for its engine. The database's owner adds Postgres's "additional" ones with CREATE EXTENSION. Some load a library, which restarts the database (`restart`). With high availability, it restarts one instance at a time and the primary hands over last. Every KV module restarts the database and needs KV 8.1. Turning a Postgres extension off drops it (DROP EXTENSION, without CASCADE). Postgres refuses while other objects depend on it, and the database's `extensions` shows this. Developers and up.

API key access: **full**.

SetServiceWafOp.title: Set service waf
SetServiceWafOp.description:
A service's web application firewall (WAF) settings, for all its domains. "log" or "block" turns it on: the WAF starts on the service's cluster with the first service there that turns it on, and stops after the last one turns it off.

level.description: How strict, 1 (fewest false alarms) to 4: the Core Rule Set's paranoia level.

exceptions.description: Rule ids not applied to this service, e.g. 942100.

threshold.description: The inbound anomaly score at which a request is blocked: 5 (the default), 10, 20 or 50.

SetTeamBackupSelectionOp.description:

exceptions.description: Service and volume ids: left out with "all", the only ones with "selected".

StartImport.description:
An import: where to (`databaseId`, or `newDatabase`), and from where
(`url`, or `uploadId`).

databaseId.description: An existing, empty database of the team's to import into.

oneOf.description: Or a new database, made for the import.

url.description: The database to copy, as a URL the cluster can reach: `postgres://user:password@host:5432/database` or `mysql://user:password@host:3306/database`, with `?sslmode=require` (or `ssl-mode=REQUIRED`), `verify-ca` or `verify-full` for TLS.

uploadId.description: Or a dump uploaded first (`createDatabaseDumpUpload`, then its file sent).

StopServiceOp.title: Stop service
StopServiceOp.description:

UpdateClusterOp.title: Update cluster
UpdateClusterOp.description:

UpdateDatabaseBackupOp.title: Update database backup
UpdateDatabaseBackupOp.description:

UpdateDatabaseOp.title: Update database
UpdateDatabaseOp.description:
Change a database's size, instances, storage, version, pooler, REST API, read replicas or deletion protection. Instances are 1 for a single server, or for high availability 2 to 8 replicas for Postgres, 2 to 4 for KV, or 2 or 4 for MySQL. MySQL instances only grow. Storage only grows and the version only goes up. Only owners and admins can turn deletion protection off. Connected services get changed variables on their next deploy.

API key access: **full**.

readReplicas.description: Dedicated read replicas, each the database's size: 1 to 5 for Postgres, or 1 to 4 for KV. 0 turns them off. They only serve reads and never become the primary. Postgres: connected services get DATABASE_URL_READ (through their own pooler) while they're on. KV: REDIS_URL sends reads to them automatically.

cpuMillis.description: With size "custom": CPU per instance in millicores (125 to 8000, steps of 125).

memoryMi.description: With size "custom": memory per instance in MiB, from 512 for Postgres, 1024 for MySQL or 256 for KV, up to 32768, in steps of 256.

UpdateFirewallRuleOp.title: Update firewall rule
UpdateFirewallRuleOp.description:

UpdateMemberRoleOp.title: Update member role
UpdateMemberRoleOp.description:

UpdateProjectOp.title: Update project

id.description: A new id you choose: `crt_` then 4 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dashes or underscores.

mustSetUp.description:
